newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Today's paper devotes five and a half pages to stories related to Hong Kong's July 1 return to Beijing rule.
- A frontpage story details how the third generation of the leadership of the Chinese Communist Party of China successfully pushed forward the process of Hong Kong's return.

- The daily frontpages a 1990 photo of Deng Xiaoping meeting members of the Committee for Drafting the Basic Law of Hong Kong to pay tribute to Deng, who initiated the idea of "one country, two systems" for solving the Hong Kong issue.

- Chinese troops to be stationed in Hong Kong are strictly following requirements set for the whole army by President Jiang Zemin that they be qualified politically, competent militarily, have a fine style of work, strict discipline and adequate logistical support.
- Hong Kong-listed First Tractor Co January-April after-tax profits rise 121.4 percent compared with the year-ago period.
- Shenzhen-listed Monkey King Co pays 30 million yuan for a controlling stake in Shenzhen Asia Diamond Co.
- Hong Kong-listed Shanghai Petrochemical Co is to take over a Zhejiang acrylic fibre producer.
- China's synthetic rubber output is seen at 900,000 tonnes by the year 2000.
- A Xinhua commentary entitled "The World Has Confidence in Hong Kong" says as the day for the return of Hong Kong approaches, the territory has become the focus of world opinion.

- China will restrict the construction of new oil refining projects and ethylene production plants until the year 2000, and will improve and expand existing refineries instead of setting up new projects.
- President Jiang Zemin is to meet British Prime Minister Tony Blair and Prince Charles before the ceremony on the handover of Hong Kong.
- Premier Li Peng says enterprise reforms should be combined with reorganisation, renovation and improved management in state-owned enterprises.
